title: Hepatitis B: Screening and Serology Interpretation

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult or child who is hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) positive: baseline tests, serology interpretation, hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) thresholds, fibrosis assessment, specialist referral, antiviral choice and monitoring, using NICE CG165.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: NICE CG165 as extracted gives no antiviral doses; peginterferon, tenofovir and entecavir doses come from product information.
Vaccination recommendations and the full contraindication list were not in the extract.
Public health screening of at-risk populations is covered in NICE guidance on hepatitis B and C testing, which was not opened.
No Saudi guideline was opened; the Saudi MOH screening programme was not checked.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: Chronic hepatitis B is HBsAg persisting for 6 months or more after acute infection; HBsAg seroconversion (anti-HBs appearing) signifies clearance. Higher HBV DNA is associated with greater risk of liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); thresholds are above 2,000 IU/ml and above 20,000 IU/ml. Abnormal ALT is 30 IU/L or more in males and 19 IU/L or more in females. Transient elastography is the initial test for liver disease in newly referred adults: 11 kPa or more is very likely cirrhosis; 6 to 10 kPa merits consideration of biopsy.

clinicalManagement.title: Baseline tests in primary care
actions: Arrange HBeAg and anti-HBe, HBV DNA, anti-HBc IgM, anti-HCV, anti-HDV, anti-HIV, anti-HAV, liver panel, full blood count, prothrombin time, liver ultrasound and alpha-fetoprotein.

clinicalManagement.title: Refer all HBsAg-positive adults
actions: Refer to a hepatologist, gastroenterologist or infectious disease specialist with test results; immediate referral if decompensated; children to a paediatric hepatologist.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess fibrosis
actions: Transient elastography first; biopsy for 6 to 10 kPa; treat without biopsy at 11 kPa or more.

clinicalManagement.title: Treat if criteria met
actions: Peginterferon alfa-2a for 48 weeks first line in compensated disease; tenofovir or entecavir as second line or in decompensated disease.

clinicalManagement.title: Monitor
actions: Untreated immune-tolerant: ALT every 24 weeks; inactive disease: ALT and HBV DNA every 48 weeks; HCC surveillance every 6 months in significant fibrosis.

medicationPlan.note: NICE CG165 sets peginterferon alfa-2a for 48 weeks as first line in compensated disease (stop consideration at 24 weeks), tenofovir disoproxil and entecavir as second-line or decompensated options with tenofovir dose reduced in renal impairment, adefovir not offered, and tenofovir for women with HBV DNA above 10^7 IU/ml in the third trimester, but the extract gives no doses. Antivirals are specialist prescriptions per the hepatology protocol. The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: HBV DNA above 2,000 IU/ml and abnormal ALT on 2 tests 3 months apart.

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: Treat regardless of age or fibrosis
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: HBV DNA above 20,000 IU/ml with abnormal ALT.
Treat if HBV DNA detectable, regardless of HBeAg, DNA or ALT levels.
Six-monthly ultrasound and alpha-fetoprotein for significant fibrosis or cirrhosis.
